In Caulfeild, West Vancouver, the 55+ homes you can buy are Nearest, outside the sub-area and Nearest, outside the sub-area (strata). The other seniors housing here, which you cannot buy into, is rental and retirement residence or care. This page names each building, says what type it is and what the sources show, and covers local rules and the questions buyers ask. Anything no source states is marked unconfirmed.
55+ strata buildings you can buy in Caulfeild
Nearest, outside the sub-area — Tudor Gardens, 843 22nd Street (Dundarave, east)

Built 1992. Building sources record age restrictions, pets not allowed and rentals not allowed, and a listing states the rule plainly: "55+ age restriction, no pets," with a large activity room, library and courtyard, one block from the seawall and across from the West Vancouver Community Centre. The "rentals not allowed" line in older building data cannot stand as a long-term rental ban under current BC law —.
Nearest, outside the sub-area — Westview Terrace, 1390 Duchess Avenue (Ambleside, east)

A North Shore realty guide lists it among West Vancouver buildings that "all have a 55+ bylaw," and a current listing describes "a quiet, well-kept 25-unit concrete building (55+)" two blocks to Ambleside village, the seawall and the beach. Treat the bylaw as listing/guide-stated and confirm it in the strata documents.
Rental, care and subsidized seniors housing in Caulfeild (not for sale)

items.t: Nearest, outside the sub-area — the Kiwanis cluster on 21st Street / Gordon Avenue (Ambleside): Kiwanis North Shore Housing Society provides independent living apartments at below-market rates for adults 55+ on the North Shore. Its West Vancouver buildings are Kiwanis Manor, 959 21st Street (labelled "55+ • WEST VANCOUVER" by the society; independent living, applications year-round, North Shore residents preferred, no pets), The Court, 2151 Gordon Avenue, The Cypress, 999 21st Street, and The Terrace, 975 21st Street. Society eligibility in its application material: capable of living independently, non-smoker, 55 or older, with income and asset limits updated annually against BC Housing's low-and-moderate income limits. Rental only — nothing to buy.

Amica West Vancouver — 659 Clyde Avenue: Registered assisted living, operator Amica West Vancouver Inc.; Amica describes private independent-living and assisted-living suites plus licensed residential care at this address.

Amica Lions Gate — Keith Road: Registered assisted living, class SN. The Registry's crawled listings give the address two ways — 727 Keith Road and 701-721 Keith Road — while the operator's own page gives 701-727 Keith Road; use the operator's range and treat the exact civic range as a minor source conflict. Amica states it offers independent living, assisted living, long-term care, memory care and respite here, and notes many of its residents come from the West Vancouver communities of Ambleside, Dundarave and British Properties.

Hollyburn House — 2095 Marine Drive: Registered assisted living, class SN, now marketed by Cogir as Venvi Hollyburn House; the operator lists independent living, assisted living, residential care, short-term and respite stays, across from the Seniors' Activity Centre and library.

Inglewood Care Centre — 725 Inglewood Avenue: Long-term care, not a purchase: opened 1979, operated by Baptist Housing Society (not for profit), 230 publicly funded beds as of March 31, 2025 per the BC Seniors Advocate's facility file. Access is through Vancouver Coastal Health assessment.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Caulfeild

items.t: Caulfeild is the District of West Vancouver's western neighbourhood: Lower Caulfeild at the foreshore, Upper Caulfeild north toward Highway 1, Lighthouse Park to the west and Marine Drive along the south. The District uses the name in Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 4985, 2018 policy for the Caulfeild Village Centre, one of its village centres alongside Dundarave and Horseshoe Bay. No street-by-street written boundary is published by the District — the exact line is UNVERIFIED. Note the spelling: the District and SD45 use "Caulfeild" (with the second "u"), not "Caulfield."

Interior streets: Caulfeild Drive, Keith Road and Headland Drive; Highway 1 (Upper Levels Highway) crosses the north side. Nearby areas: Lighthouse Park (west), Altamont and West Bay (east), Cypress Park Estates (north, across Highway 1).

The area has both schools inside it: Caulfeild Elementary (iDEC), 4685 Keith Road (K–7), and Rockridge Secondary, 5350 Headland Drive (8–12), across from Caulfeild Village. SD45 catchments are address-based; the locator result for the sample address 4685 Keith Road is Caulfeild Elementary and Rockridge Secondary, and SD45 has no middle tier.

Parks: Caulfeild Park offers the Caulfeild Trail, rocky foreshore, sandy beaches and swimming in calm, protected water; Lighthouse Park at the west edge has trails through old-growth forest to the historic lighthouse.

Transit: TransLink route 253 (Caulfeild Village / Park Royal), operated as West Vancouver Blue Bus, runs via Caulfeild Drive, Cherbourg Drive, Keith Road and Marine Drive, with select trips continuing to Vancouver via the Lions Gate Bridge; route 262 runs from Caulfeild Village to Horseshoe Bay, Lions Bay and Brunswick Beach, and route 250 runs on Marine Drive.

Health care: Lions Gate Hospital, 231 East 15th Street, North Vancouver, is the Vancouver Coastal Health hospital serving the North Shore including West Vancouver; the North Vancouver Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at Suite 200, 221 West Esplanade, North Vancouver.

Shopping: Caulfeild Village Centre is the commercial centre named in OCP Policy 2.3.4 — store names and addresses inside it are UNVERIFIED (not confirmed on a District source). The District's main recreation and library facilities are east in Ambleside: the West Vancouver Community Centre and Aquatic Centre, 2121 Marine Drive, and West Vancouver Memorial Library, 1950 Marine Drive, beside the Seniors' Activity Centre at 695 21st Street.

blocks.text: Local rules and plans in Caulfeild

items.t: Caulfeild zoning: CD86 (Caulfeild Zone) in Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010: set by Amendment Bylaw No. 5321, 2024, replacing the former Caulfeild Land Use Contract. CD86 has Residential Area A, Residential Area B, a Commercial Area and a Parks and Greenspaces Area; the minimum permitted site area for a residential parcel is the site area lawfully registered on the parcel; Residential Area A density is a maximum of three dwelling units per lot, and stratification of buildings or land is prohibited in Residential Area A — the zoning reason no 55+ strata can exist in that part of Caulfeild.

Nearby RS zones: state minimum site areas of 8,094 m² in RS1, 1,625 m² in RS2, 975 m² in RS3, 731 m² in RS4 and 488 m² in RS5, with secondary suites and detached secondary suites among permitted uses; the bylaw's ground-oriented rules allow 4 dwellings per lot, or 6 within 400 metres of a prescribed bus stop — outside CD86 Area A, subject to each lot's zone.

Heritage: Lower Caulfeild is a designated Heritage Conservation Area — Francis Caulfeild planned the subdivision from 1899 — and owners within the area need a Heritage Alteration Permit for any work. That permit layer applies to the suite/coach-house "stay in place" route in Lower Caulfeild.

Hazard permits: an Environmental Development Permit applies within 15 metres of the top of a watercourse bank, a Wildfire Hazard Development Permit within 100 metres of an undisturbed forest interface, and a Foreshore Development Permit on waterfront/coastal-flood-risk lots — all three can apply in Caulfeild, the foreshore one on Lower Caulfeild waterfront lots.

District and provincial policy context: the OCP, Bylaw No. 4985, 2018, names the Caulfeild Village Centre in Policy 2.3.4, and on December 1, 2025 Council adopted OCP Amendment Bylaw No. 5406, 2025, aligning the OCP with the 2024 Interim Housing Needs Report. The District's own reporting states seniors rose from about one in five residents in 2001 to nearly one in three in 2021 (median age 51 in 2021), with the OCP aiming for more seniors and rental housing options — none of it directed at Caulfeild specifically in the sources checked.

Taxes: District of West Vancouver 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on unpaid current taxes on July 2, 2026 and a further 5% on outstanding current taxes on September 2, 2026. At Caulfeild price points the Province's additional school tax can apply — 0.2% on the residential portion of assessed value between $3 million and $4 million and 0.4% above $4 million for 2026, rising to 0.3% and 0.6% on January 1, 2027. Water and sewer are metered and billed quarterly.

items.t: BC 55+ strata rules

Caulfeild's zoning literally bans the product this page is about: since Amendment Bylaw No. 5321, 2024 created CD86, stratification is prohibited in Residential Area A of the old Land Use Contract lands — so no condo, townhouse strata or 55+ complex can be created there, whatever demand does. The area's one strata, Caulfeild Cove on Marine Drive, predates that structure (built 1974) and carries no age bylaw in any source checked.

The Land Use Contract era just ended here: CD86 replaced the Caulfeild Land Use Contract in 2024 — the area's most recent District-significant land-use change — and Residential Area A's minimum site area is simply whatever was lawfully registered on each parcel, so lot-by-lot history matters more than a zone table.

Lower Caulfeild's heritage rules are a second permit system: the designated Heritage Conservation Area (subdivision planned by Francis Caulfeild from 1899) requires a Heritage Alteration Permit for any work — a cost and timeline factor for any senior planning to adapt a Lower Caulfeild house for aging in place.

The whole District has only three buildings a North Shore guide lists as 55+-bylaw strata — Westview Terrace (1390 Duchess Ave), Tudor Gardens (843 22nd St) and Lincoln Gardens (address not stated on the guide page — UNCONFIRMED here) — all in Ambleside/Dundarave. A Caulfeild downsizer's realistic choice is: one of those, a Kiwanis rental on 21st Street, an Amica/Hollyburn residence, or staying put with a suite and services.

The District's big seniors build is the Inglewood redevelopment, east of here: on September 21, 2026, Council approved the two-phase redevelopment of Inglewood Care Centre (725 Inglewood Ave) — Phase 1, a 364-bed publicly funded long-term care facility; Phase 2, 200 independent-living units and 161 seniors rental housing units. The District does not handle tenant placement; Baptist Housing does.

Kiwanis Manor carries two descriptions in two sources — independent 55+ rental on the society's site, registered assisted living in BC's Assisted Living Registry under a partnership name. Confirm which product it actually offers before describing it to a client.

Both of Caulfeild's schools are inside the area, which keeps family demand — and family pricing — under senior sellers' houses: Caulfeild Elementary (4685 Keith Rd) and Rockridge Secondary (5350 Headland Dr) are a matched K–12 pair in one pocket, rare in West Vancouver (Altamont and Chelsea Park have no school inside the pocket at all).

faq.q: What 55+ homes can I actually buy in Caulfeild?
faq.a: None inside the area — no verified 55+ strata exists in Caulfeild, and in the CD86 Residential Area A lands stratification is prohibited outright. The nearest verified 55+ ownership buildings are east in Dundarave and Ambleside: Tudor Gardens, 843 22nd St, and Westview Terrace, 1390 Duchess Ave.

faq.q: Is Caulfeild Cove a seniors complex? It looks like downsizer product.
faq.a: No age restriction appears in any source checked for Caulfeild Cove (4957 Marine Dr, 30 townhouse units, built 1974): building sources record pets allowed and rentals not allowed, and nothing about age. It is a general-market strata — any age can live there.

faq.q: Could a Caulfeild strata vote in a 55+ bylaw later?
faq.a: In BC a strata can adopt a 55+ age bylaw under Strata Property Act ss. 123.1–123.2 — that is the only age bylaw now permitted — but residents already living in a unit when such a bylaw passes are protected as legacy residents under Strata Property Regulation 7.01. Whether Caulfeild Cove has ever considered one is UNCONFIRMED.

faq.q: If I stay in my Caulfeild house, can I add a suite or coach house instead of moving?
faq.a: It depends which side of the zoning line the lot sits on: CD86 Residential Area A allows a maximum of three dwelling units per lot but prohibits stratification (so added units cannot be sold separately); RS-zone lots nearby list secondary suites and detached secondary suites as permitted uses. In Lower Caulfeild, any work also needs a Heritage Alteration Permit.

faq.q: Is there a 55+ rental building near Caulfeild?
faq.a: Yes, in Ambleside: the Kiwanis North Shore Housing Society's West Vancouver buildings (Kiwanis Manor, 959 21st St; The Court, 2151 Gordon Ave; The Cypress, 999 21st St; The Terrace, 975 21st St) are independent-living rentals for 55+, below-market, with income/asset eligibility, preference for North Shore residents, and no pets. Rental only.

faq.q: Are pets allowed in the nearest 55+ options?
faq.a: Tudor Gardens is recorded as no pets, and Kiwanis seniors communities do not permit pets; Caulfeild Cove (not 55+) records pets allowed. Westview Terrace's pet position is UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked.

faq.q: Where is the hospital, and what if I need care later?
faq.a: Lions Gate Hospital, 231 East 15th Street, North Vancouver, serves the North Shore including West Vancouver. The in-District care ladder is east in Ambleside: registered assisted living at Amica West Vancouver (659 Clyde Ave), Amica Lions Gate (Keith Rd) and Hollyburn House (2095 Marine Dr), then long-term care at Inglewood Care Centre (725 Inglewood Ave, 230 publicly funded beds). None of it is in Caulfeild.

faq.q: What transit can a Caulfeild senior actually use?
faq.a: Route 253 links Caulfeild Village to Park Royal with select trips through to downtown Vancouver over the Lions Gate Bridge; route 262 links the village to Horseshoe Bay and Lions Bay; route 250 runs on Marine Drive. It is bus-served but car-oriented for most daily trips.
